newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN Council concerned on Mideast but puts off action.
newsitem.headline: UN Council concerned on Mideast but puts off action.

text.p: U.N. Security Council members on Friday expressed concern about the deteriorating situation between Israel and the Palestinians, but rejected any formal statement at this time.
"There is no immediate intention to continue that discussion as far as the presidency is aware," Council President Sir John Weston of Britain told reporters after informal consultations.
Palestinians leaders on Monday called on the council to protest Israeli measures against the Palestinians on the West Bank and Gaza, touched off by a suicide bombing last week.

But diplomats said Arab delegations put off pushing for a formal council declaration from the council, which the United States opposed, until U.S. special envoy Denis Ross returns from the region. He is expected to go there this weekend.

Secretary of State Madeleine Albright might also go the Middle East at the end of August, depending on security, in an effort to bring forward talks on the shape of a final Israeli-Palestinian peace settlement.
Weston said many but not all council members voiced concern "by recent actions and measures taken by Israel which threatened to impose serious hardships on the Palestinians."

Members in their informal discussions expressed concern about the deteriorating situation in the Middle East and again condemned in suicide bombings "which enforces the urgency of a return to negotiations," he said.
They wanted all parties to commit themselves unconditionally in preventing further violence, resumption of the peace process and timely implementation of agreements already reached, he added.

Nassir al-Kidwa, the Palestinian observer at the United Nations, said he had hoped for stronger action but said he believed the council had "sent a clear message of serious concern" to Israel while waiting for events to develop.

The bombings in Jerusalem on July 30 killed 15 people including the two Arab attackers, and plunged Palestinain leader Yasser Arafat's relations with Israel's right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to an all-time low.

Israel has suspended peace talks and sealed off the West Bank and Gaza Strip, disrupting Palestinian trade and preventing tens of thousands of Arab workers from reaching their jobs in the Jewish state.
